problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose that $V=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$ Given that $B={{a}_{1},{a}_{2},b}$ is an orthogonal basis for $V,{a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-(\frac{0}{4})[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-(-\frac{40}{20})[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=3,$ $c=3,$ and $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{3}{3}=1.$
